s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic painful intertriginous wounds with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques
Granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate with well-formed, nonnecrotizing granulomas
key_facts: 1.5-year history of painful intertriginous wounds
History of hypertension and depression
Multiple hospital admissions for cellulitis around the wounds
Received diverting sigmoid colostomy and indwelling urinary catheter
Wound care required nursing home care
No clinical improvement with adalimumab
Family history of similar condition
Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques in intertriginous areas
Histopathology showed pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate
Laboratory tests negative for infections and autoimmune disorders
Elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies and flagellins

shortlist.label: Intertriginous granulomatous dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of painful intertriginous wounds with granulomatous inflammation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies and flagellins, and history of diverting sigmoid colostomy

shortlist.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
shortlist.why_kept: Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques in intertriginous areas

shortlist.label: Blau syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar condition and granulomatous inflammation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate on histopathology and negative laboratory tests for infections

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques in intertriginous areas, along with histopathology showing pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate, is more consistent with intertriginous granulomatous dermatitis. The lack of gastrointestinal involvement and negative laboratory tests for infections and autoimmune disorders also support this diagnosis.
raw.anchor_refutation: Crohn's disease is less likely due to the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms and unremarkable imaging studies of the gastrointestinal tract. The patient's response to adalimumab, a treatment for Crohn's disease, was also poor, further refuting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: Lack of gastrointestinal symptoms and poor response to adalimumab

rejected.label: Hidradenitis suppurativa
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and histopathology are not typical of hidradenitis suppurativa

rejected.label: Blau syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of systemic symptoms make Blau syndrome less likely

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory tests do not support a diagnosis of sarcoidosis
